title: MSA/DPA Fast-Triage: Liability Exposure Forecast & Sales Quote Adjuster
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build an automated triage and scoring engine that ingests MSA/DPA redlines and security questionnaire answers to produce: 1) a liability exposure forecast (expected indemnity/liability uplift relative to baseline), 2) a recommended sales quote adjuster (price delta and approval path), and 3) a structured summary for legal review. Goal: reduce average legal triage time from 3 business days to <8 business hours for low/medium risk deals and enable sales to generate pre-approved adjusted quotes at point-of-signing.
success_metrics: Reduce legal triage median time to <8 business hours for low/medium risk
Increase percentage of self-servable enterprise quotes from 12% to 45%
Accuracy: legal sign-off rate on engine recommendations >= 85%
Decrease average negotiated indemnity cap uplift by 20% in pilot accounts
approach: Phase 1: Rules-based triage using clause fingerprinting and security QA mappings
Phase 2: Liability scoring model calibrated from historical concessions and legal outcomes
Phase 3: UI for sales to preview adjusted quote with justification and approval path
Phase 4: Integrate with Contract Intake queue and Sales CRM to surface recommendations
acceptance_criteria: Engine identifies contract clauses and maps to risk buckets with >=90% precision in test set
Sales UI surfaces recommended quote delta and approval steps; legal approves in pilot accounts
Audit log generated linking redline => score => recommendation for compliance
notes: Work surfaced from heavy manual burden during recent ARR ramp with enterprise deals. Legal provided anonymized concession history and example redlines for modeling. Initial pilot customers include two AI-native startups and a mid-market SaaS customer who requested faster quote turnaround.
comments: 2025-01-16 - Aisha Patel: Kickoff with Legal and Sales Ops. Shared data export template for historical concessions. Action: Legal to provide anonymized MSA/DPA redlines (due 2025-01-22).

2025-01-23 - Liam O'Connor: Received dataset (140 redlines + concession outcomes). Preliminary ETL notes: inconsistent clause labels, will run fuzzy fingerprinting. Estimate updated: +1 point for cleaning.

2025-01-28 - Legal (Maya Chen): Feedback on clause mapping — prefer ‘indemnity-cap’ and ‘jurisdiction-waiver’ as separate flags. Also flagged two common non-negotiable clauses. Action: include override flags in scoring model.

2025-01-30 - Engineering (Diego Rivera): PoC rules engine completed. Early precision on clause detection 78% on raw data; improved to 92% after synonym normalization. Next: integrate with pricing simulator microservice.
2025-02-02 - Sales (Rajiv Menon): Reviewed UI mock. Request: make quote delta presented as absolute $ and percent, include suggested negotiation script. Will pilot with two SDRs.

2025-02-03 - Aisha Patel: Decision to phase rollout. Phase 1 (rules + sales UI) to pilot with three deals. Phase 2 will expand with ML-calibrated scoring if we hit precision and legal sign-off thresholds.
implementation_notes: Prototype lives in microservice 'contracts-triage' with a rules engine component and a small feature-flagged UI in Console. We will record telemetry for model drift and false positives and add an admin override audit trail. Consider data retention for exported redlines per compliance guidance.
risks: Model/Rules drift if legal clause language changes rapidly
Sales overreliance leading to approval bypass risk
Data sensitivity — need to ensure anonymized training pipeline and KMS for exported artifacts
next_steps: Legal to sign off on initial clause taxonomy (due 2025-02-06)
Engineering to deploy feature-flagged UI to staging (due 2025-02-10)
Schedule pilot with Sales Ops and two customer reps (target week of 2025-02-17)
